mainTopic: The shape of the קרשים of the משכן (tapered or even, רבי יהודה vs. רבי נחמיה) and how this changes the way the curtains covered the משכן.
overview: This amud opens with שמואל finishing an earlier question about the wagons of the משכן: what lay under them was the narrow stakes (יתדות). Then a ברייתא brings a מחלוקת about the beams (קרשים). רבי יהודה says they narrowed to a fingerbreadth at the top. רבי נחמיה says they stayed one אמה thick all the way up. Each side explains the other's word in the פסוק (תמים, יחדו), and רבי יהודה answers a challenge from the corner beams by saying the beams were sloped like mountains. A ברייתא adds that the middle bar (בריח התיכון) stood by a miracle. The גמרא then measures the inner curtains and the goat-hair curtains and shows how much of the beams and sockets each view leaves covered or showing. The extra back curtain leads to a question on רבי נחמיה from the word תסרח, which he reads as 'hangs longer than the others.' The amud ends by starting a new ברייתא about grooved beams and hollow sockets, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל: The Stakes Were Under the Wagons
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers the earlier question about the wagons: the items stored there were the narrow יתדות (stakes), so the space under the wagons stayed open.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It was with the stakes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question on the previous amud. It had asked how the space under the wagons of the משכן could count as open public space, and שמואל answers that it was the stakes that were placed there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the wagons were loaded with wide beams, which would cover the space underneath. שמואל says the stakes, which are narrow, were set down first, so the gaps between them were big enough that the area underneath stayed an uncovered רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: Stakes or pegs used in setting up the משכן.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: With the stakes.
phrases.notes: This answers a question raised on the previous amud about the space under the wagons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a question earlier about the wagons of the משכן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the items placed there were narrow stakes, not wide beams.
steps.terutzMaskana: The space under the wagons stayed open because only stakes were set down there.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: The Beams Narrowed to a Fingerbreadth at the Top
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי יהודה's view: the קרשים were one אמה thick at the bottom and thinned out to a fingerbreadth at the top, learned from the word תמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The beams were one cubit thick at the bottom, and at the top they kept getting thinner until they were like a finger, as it says, 'they will be תמים at its top.' And elsewhere it says 'תמו נכרתו' (they ended, they were cut off). These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about the shape of the beams of the משכן. This step gives the first opinion, רבי יהודה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the word תמים as 'coming to an end.' He proves this meaning from a פסוק in יהושע, where תמו means the waters 'ended.' So the beams tapered at the top until they almost came to an end, leaving just a fingerbreadth.

keyTerms.meaning: The upright wooden beams that formed the walls of the משכן.
Gradually getting smaller, narrowing more and more.
From the פסוק; רבי יהודה reads it as 'ending' or 'finishing.'
'And elsewhere,' meaning another פסוק that uses the same word.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The beams were one cubit thick at the bottom,
and at the top they kept narrowing until they were like a fingerbreadth,
as it says: 'They will be tamim at its top' (Shemos 26:24),
and elsewhere it says: 'They ended, they were cut off' (Yehoshua 3:16).
phrases.notes: This shows that the root תמם means 'to end.'

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קְרָשִׁים מִלְּמַטָּן עוֹבְיָין אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the shape of the beams.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beams were one אמה thick at the bottom and tapered to a fingerbreadth at the top (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: The Beams Were One Cubit Thick All the Way Up
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה disagrees: the beams were one אמה thick at the top just like at the bottom, learned from the word יחדיו (together).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: Just as they were one cubit thick at the bottom, so too they were one cubit thick at the top, as it says: 'Together.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the second opinion. רבי נחמיה holds that the beams did not taper at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה reads יחדיו ('together') to mean the top and bottom of each beam were the same. So the thickness stayed one אמה the whole way up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Just as... so too,' used to compare two things as equal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:
Just as they were one cubit thick at the bottom,
so too they were one cubit thick at the top,
as it says: 'Together.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּלְּמַטָּן עוֹבְיָין אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beams were one אמה thick at both the top and the bottom (רבי נחמיה).
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says the beams tapered (from תמים). רבי נחמיה says they stayed even (from יחדיו). Each opinion will now need to explain the other side's word.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי נחמיה: What About the Word תמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבי נחמיה: the פסוק says תמים, which רבי יהודה used to prove the beams tapered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי נחמיה. If the beams did not taper, what does the word תמים come to teach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the פסוק must mean something. רבי נחמיה needs his own explanation for תמים, or else רבי יהודה's reading wins.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it written...?', which introduces a challenge from a פסוק.

phrases.english: But isn't it written 'Tamim'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי נחמיה using רבי יהודה's source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נחמיה's view that the beams were even.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word תמים seems to mean 'ending,' which points to tapering. What does רבי נחמיה do with it?

steps.title: Answer: תמים Means Whole Beams, Not Joined Planks
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה explains תמים as 'whole': each beam had to be one solid piece, not boards joined together.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word teaches that they should bring whole beams, and not bring planks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי נחמיה. He reads תמים as 'complete' instead of 'ending.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמים can also mean 'whole' or 'complete.' So the פסוק teaches that each beam was one solid piece of wood, not planks attached together. It says nothing about tapering.

phrases.english: That word teaches that they should bring whole beams
and not bring planks.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תמים means 'ending,' so the beams tapered.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי נחמיה, תמים means 'whole': each beam was one solid piece.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי יהודה: What About the Word יחדו?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks the other side: according to רבי יהודה, the פסוק says יחדו, which רבי נחמיה used to prove the beams were even.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written 'Together'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same question around. If רבי יהודה says the beams tapered, what does יחדו come to teach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as רבי נחמיה had to explain תמים, רבי יהודה must explain יחדו. Otherwise it sounds like the top and bottom were the same.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the other one,' meaning the other opinion.

phrases.english: And the other one too, isn't it written 'Together'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the challenge of step 4, now aimed at רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that the beams tapered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יחדו implies the top and bottom matched. What does רבי יהודה do with it?

steps.title: Answer: יחדו Means the Beams Were Lined Up Straight
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains יחדו as an instruction that the beams must stand perfectly aligned, not crooked.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word teaches that they should not be skewed from one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה. יחדו is about how the beams stood next to each other, not about their thickness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Together' here means the beams stood neatly in a straight row, with none sticking out of line. So it does not prove the top was as thick as the bottom.

keyTerms.meaning: They should be shifted or skewed out of line.

phrases.english: That word teaches that they should not be skewed from one another.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יחדו means the top and bottom were equally thick.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, יחדו means the beams were aligned straight.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions keep both words of the פסוק. They just read them differently: תמים means 'tapering' or 'whole,' and יחדו means 'equal thickness' or 'aligned.'

steps.title: Challenge to רבי יהודה from the Corner Beams
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the corner beams of the back wall fit perfectly for רבי נחמיה, but for רבי יהודה a tapering beam would leave the corner uneven, with one beam going in and one sticking out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says the beams were one cubit thick at the top just like at the bottom. That explains why it is written: 'For the back of the משכן westward make six beams, and make two beams for the corners.' The width of these corner beams comes and fills in the thickness of those side beams. But for the one who says they were one cubit thick at the bottom and narrowed to a fingerbreadth at the top, this one goes in and this one sticks out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses a בשלמא structure: one view fits the פסוקים, and the other seems to have a problem. Here the problem is aimed at רבי יהודה, from how the corners of the משכן were built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The back wall had two extra corner beams. Part of their width covered the end of the side walls, which were one אמה thick, making a neat, flush corner. If the beams were even, this fits perfectly at every height. But if they tapered, the side wall gets thinner going up while the corner beam stays the same, so at the top one part sinks in and another sticks out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works well for...' This sets up a contrast in which the other view will be challenged.
'Goes in... goes out,' meaning uneven and sticking out.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two measurements. פותיא is the width of a beam (side to side along the wall). סומכא is its thickness (from inside the משכן to outside). The corner beam's width covers the side beam's thickness.

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says
that just as they were one cubit thick at the bottom
so too they were one cubit thick at the top,
this explains what is written:
'And for the back of the Mishkan, westward,
you shall make six beams.
And two beams you shall make for the corners' (Shemos 26:22–23).
meaning the width of these comes
and fills in the thickness of those.
But according to the one who says
they were one cubit thick at the bottom
and at the top they narrowed until a fingerbreadth,
this one goes in and this one sticks out!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּלְּמַטָּן עוֹבְיָין אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the word-based challenges, the גמרא brings a structural challenge against רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that the beams tapered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tapering side beams can't meet the even corner beams flush, so the corner would be uneven.

steps.title: Answer: The Beams Were Shaved into a Slope Like Mountains
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה, the beams were also shaved into a slope, like a mountainside, so the corners matched and nothing stuck out.
steps.simpleTranslation: They shaved them down, like mountains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה. The corner pieces were also sloped to match the tapering, so nothing stuck out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem only exists if the corner beams stayed full width while the side beams thinned. The answer is that the beams were shaved into a matching slope, like the side of a mountain. Then the corner stays smooth at every height, and רבי יהודה's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Mountains, meaning sloped like a mountainside.

phrases.english: They shaved them down like mountains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the corner challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a detail about how the beams were made that removes the problem.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tapering beams would leave the corners uneven.
steps.terutzMaskana: The beams were also sloped like mountains, so the corners matched even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions survive. רבי יהודה holds the beams tapered and were sloped like mountains, so the corners still fit. רבי נחמיה holds the beams were one אמה thick all the way up.

steps.title: The middle bar stood by a miracle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the middle bar (בריח התיכון) running through the beams stayed in place by a miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the middle bar in the midst of the beams.' A ברייתא taught: it stood by a miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more teaching about the beams: the long middle bar that ran through them was held up by a miracle. After this, the גמרא moves on to the curtains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle bar went through the inside of the beams along all three walls of the משכן. One straight bar cannot turn corners on its own, so the ברייתא says it stayed in place through a נס.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle bar that ran through the inside of the beams

phrases.english: "And the middle bar in the midst of the beams"
It was taught: it stood by a miracle.
phrases.notes: It bent around the corners of the three walls without any natural support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more detail about the beams before the גמרא turns to the curtains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בריח התיכון stayed in place miraculously.

steps.title: Inner curtains across the width: what was left uncovered on the sides
steps.stepSummary: The inner curtains were 28 אמות long. Laid across the 10-אמה roof, 9 hung down each side. For רבי יהודה the socket אמה showed. For רבי נחמיה one אמה of the beams showed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall make the משכן with ten curtains... the length of each curtain is twenty-eight אמות.' Lay their length across the width of the משכן. How much is it? Twenty-eight. Take away ten for the roof. Nine are left for this side and nine for that side. For רבי יהודה, the אמה of the sockets is left showing. For רבי נחמיה, an אמה of the beams is left showing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the math for the first layer of curtains, laid across the width of the משכן. It shows how the result changes between רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are 28 אמות of curtain. The roof uses 10, so 9 hang down each side. The beams are 10 tall, and their bottom אמה sits inside the silver sockets (אדנים). For רבי יהודה, the narrow beam tops take no curtain, so 9 hang down and cover the beam all the way to the socket, leaving only the socket showing. For רבי נחמיה, the full-אמה-thick top of each side wall uses 1 אמה, so only 8 hang down, and one אמה of the beam itself is left showing above the socket.

keyTerms.meaning: The silver sockets the beams stood in

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא says to subtract only 10 for the roof, but for רבי נחמיה the thick beam tops also use up 1 אמה on each side. That hidden extra אמה is why his result is different. It comes from the earlier argument about the beam shape.

phrases.english: "And you shall make the Tabernacle with ten curtains ...

phrases.aramaic: אֹרֶךְ הַיְרִיעָה הָאַחַת שְׁמֹנֶה וְעֶשְׂרִים בָּאַמָּה״.
phrases.english: the length of each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits."
Lay their length across the width of the Tabernacle.
How much is it? Twenty-eight.
Take away ten for the roof.
phrases.notes: The inside width of the משכן was 10 אמות.

phrases.aramaic: פָּשׁוּ לְהוּ תֵּשַׁע לְהַאי גִּיסָא וְתֵשַׁע לְהַאי גִּיסָא.
phrases.english: Nine are left for this side and nine for that side.
For Rabbi Yehuda, the cubit of the sockets is exposed.
phrases.notes: The 9 hanging down cover the beam above the socket.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Nechemya, a cubit of the beams is exposed.
phrases.notes: The thick beam top uses 1 אמה, so only 8 hang down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the beam-shape argument to how the inner curtains covered the sides.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Across the width: for רבי יהודה the sockets show; for רבי נחמיה the sockets and one אמה of beam show.

steps.title: Inner curtains along the length: what hung down the back wall
steps.stepSummary: Ten curtains, each 4 אמות wide, make 40 אמות. The roof uses 30, leaving 10 for the back. For רבי יהודה the sockets are covered. For רבי נחמיה they are showing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lay their width along the length of the משכן. How much is it? Forty. Take away thirty for the roof. Ten are left. For רבי יהודה, the אמה of the sockets is covered. For רבי נחמיה, the אמה of the sockets is showing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now does the same math in the other direction: the combined width of the curtains along the length of the משכן, toward the back wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten curtains, 4 אמות wide each, make 40 אמות. The roof is 30 long, so 10 hang down the back wall. The front was an open entrance, so nothing hangs there. For רבי יהודה, all 10 hang down and cover even the socket. For רבי נחמיה, the thick top of the back wall uses 1 אמה, so 9 hang down and the socket shows.

phrases.english: Lay their width along the length of the Tabernacle.
How much is it? Forty.
Take away thirty for the roof.
Ten are left,
phrases.notes: These hang down the back wall only. The front was the open entrance.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yehuda, the cubit of the sockets is covered.
For Rabbi Nechemya, the cubit of the sockets is exposed.
phrases.notes: The thick back-wall top uses 1 אמה, so only 9 hang down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same calculation as step 11, in the other direction (along the length).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Along the length: for רבי יהודה the back sockets are covered; for רבי נחמיה they show.

steps.title: Goat-hair curtains across the width: covering the sides
steps.stepSummary: The goat-hair curtains were 30 אמות long. Laid across the 10-אמה roof, 10 hung down each side. For רבי יהודה the sockets are covered. For רבי נחמיה they are showing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall make curtains of goat hair for a tent... the length of each curtain is thirty אמות.' Lay their length across the width of the משכן. How much is it? Thirty. Take away ten for the roof. Ten are left for this side and ten for that side. For רבי יהודה, the אמה of the sockets is covered. For רבי נחמיה, the אמה of the sockets is showing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the same math for the second, outer layer: the goat-hair curtains, laid across the width of the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are 30 אמות of curtain. The roof uses 10, so 10 hang down each side. For רבי יהודה, all 10 hang down and cover the whole beam plus the socket. For רבי נחמיה, the thick beam top uses 1 אמה, so 9 hang down and the socket shows.
steps.whatToRemember: Every curtain calculation comes back to one point. For רבי יהודה, the narrow beam tops take no curtain, so more hangs down. For רבי נחמיה, the thick tops use 1 אמה on each wall, so each wall is covered 1 אמה less.

phrases.english: "And you shall make curtains of goat hair for a tent, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אֹרֶךְ הַיְרִיעָה הָאַחַת שְׁלֹשִׁים בָּאַמָּה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: the length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, etc."
Lay their length across the width of the Tabernacle.
How much is it? Thirty.
Take away ten for the roof.

phrases.aramaic: פָּשׁוּ לְהוּ עֲשַׂר לְהַאי גִּיסָא וַעֲשַׂר לְהַאי גִּיסָא.
phrases.english: Ten are left for this side and ten for that side.
For Rabbi Yehuda, the cubit of the sockets is covered.
For Rabbi Nechemya, the cubit of the sockets is exposed.
phrases.notes: The thick beam top uses 1 אמה, so only 9 hang down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same method to the second layer (goat-hair curtains).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Goat-hair curtains across the width: for רבי יהודה the sockets are covered; for רבי נחמיה they show.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up the dispute about the extra אמה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק about the extra אמה on each side. רבי יהודה says it covers the sockets. רבי נחמיה says it covers the beams.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also taught this. The פסוק says "and the אמה on this side and the אמה on that side, from the extra." רבי יהודה says this extra is to cover the אמה of the sockets. רבי נחמיה says it is to cover the אמה of the beams.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the calculation from the last step about the goat-hair curtains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 worked out that the goat-hair curtains hang 10 אמות down each side. The פסוק talks about one extra אמה on each side, and the ברייתא says what that אמה covers. For רבי יהודה it reaches the sockets. For רבי נחמיה it only reaches the bottom of the beams, so the sockets stay showing, just as step 13 said.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)
The silver sockets the beams stood in
The wooden beams that made the walls of the משכן

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
"And the cubit on this side and the cubit on that side, of what remains"
to cover the cubit of the sockets,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: לְכַסּוֹת אַמָּה שֶׁל קְרָשִׁים.
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says: to cover the cubit of the beams.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 13's result for the goat-hair curtains with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That the goat-hair curtains cover the sockets for רבי יהודה but only the beams for רבי נחמיה

steps.title: Measuring the goat-hair curtains along the length of the משכן
steps.stepSummary: Eleven goat-hair curtains, each 4 אמות wide, make 44 אמות. Take away 30 for the roof, then 2 for folding the sixth curtain, and 12 are left for the back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lay their width along the length of the משכן. How much is it? 44. Take away 30 for the roof, and 14 are left. Take away 2 for the fold, as the פסוק says "and you shall double the sixth curtain over the front of the tent." Now 12 are left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the math for the goat-hair curtains going from front to back, and finds 12 אמות hanging down the back wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are 11 goat-hair curtains (one more than the 10 inner ones), so together they are 44 אמות wide. The roof is 30 long, and 2 אמות are folded over the front entrance, so 12 hang down the back. This number sets up the next question about the word תסרח.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 12. There it was the 10 inner curtains (40 אמות). Here it is the 11 goat-hair curtains (44 אמות).

phrases.english: Lay their width along the length of the Tabernacle,
how much is it? Forty-four.
Take away thirty for the roof,
fourteen are left.
Take away two for the fold,
as it is written: "And you shall double the sixth curtain
over the front of the tent"
twelve are left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sides of the goat-hair curtains to the back
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The goat-hair curtains leave 12 אמות hanging down the back of the משכן

steps.title: How does רבי נחמיה explain the word תסרח?
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה, part of the back curtain lies on the ground, so the פסוק's word "trail" fits. For רבי נחמיה, what does "trail" mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי יהודה. That is why the פסוק says "half the extra curtain shall trail." But for רבי נחמיה, what does "trail" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי נחמיה from a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the beams narrow to almost nothing at the top, so no curtain is used up there. The wall with its sockets is 10 אמות tall, so 10 of the 12 cover it and 2 drag on the ground. Those 2 are exactly half of a 4-אמה curtain, which matches "half the extra curtain shall trail." For רבי נחמיה, 1 אמה is used up covering the thick top of the back wall, so only 1 אמה drags. That is not half a curtain, so what does תסרח describe?

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (opens a contrast: fine for one side, hard for the other)
That is why it is written

phrases.english: It works well according to Rabbi Yehuda,
that is why it is written:
"Half the extra curtain shall trail."
But according to Rabbi Nechemya, what does "shall trail" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 12-אמה number to test each view against the פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נחמיה's view of the beams
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In his view only 1 אמה of the back curtain trails, not 'half the extra curtain' (2 אמות), so the פסוק's תסרח does not fit

steps.title: תסרח means it hangs longer than the others
steps.stepSummary: For רבי נחמיה, "trail" means the back curtain hangs down more than the curtains on the other sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Trail" means it hangs down more than its fellows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי נחמיה by reading the word תסרח differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תסרח does not have to mean dragging on the ground. It can mean hanging lower than the rest. For רבי נחמיה, after the thick beam tops are covered, 11 אמות hang down the back but only 9 on each side. So the back hangs 2 אמות longer, which is the 'half curtain' that the פסוק calls תסרח.

keyTerms.meaning: Than its fellows (more than the other parts of the curtain)

phrases.english: It trails more than its fellows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי נחמיה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תסרח means the curtain drags on the ground
steps.terutzMaskana: תסרח means it hangs longer than the curtains on the other sides

steps.title: The משכן is like a woman whose skirt trails behind her
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל compares the משכן to a woman walking in the market with her skirt trailing behind her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: What is the משכן like? It is like a woman walking in the market with her skirts trailing after her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a picture that shows how the back curtain looked, hanging longer than the sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The front of the משכן had the short folded part. The back had the longest overhang. This is like a dress that is shorter in front and trails behind, which fits the idea that the back curtain hangs more than the others.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
What is it like? (opens a comparison)
Her skirts, the bottom of her dress

steps.whatToRemember: The back of the משכן had the longest overhang (12 אמות). For רבי יהודה, 2 אמות (half a curtain) trailed on the ground. For רבי נחמיה, only 1 אמה trailed, so he reads תסרח as 'hangs more than the others,' since the back hung 2 אמות longer than the sides.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
To what is the Tabernacle similar?
To a woman walking in the marketplace
with her skirts trailing after her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a picture of the longer trailing back curtain
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משכן's back curtain trailed like the skirt of a woman's dress

steps.title: A new ברייתא: grooved beams and hollow sockets
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא begins: the beams were grooved at the bottom, and the sockets were hollow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The beams were grooved and the sockets were hollow,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about how the beams fit into the sockets. This is a setup line, and the ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from the curtains to how the walls were built. The bottom of each beam was cut with grooves, and the sockets were hollow so the grooved parts could slide into them and hold the beams up.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The beams were grooved
and the sockets were hollow,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the curtains to how the beams stood in the sockets
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beams had grooved bottoms that fit into the hollow sockets
